records.title: Education-record disclosure consent and use limitation
records.applicability_trigger: A district discloses real education records to SSLS under the school-official exception.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. SSLS holds no education records and has no district customer.
records.future_phase_applicability: On first district data-sharing agreement, SSLS becomes a party acting for the institution and inherits use and re-disclosure limits.
records.subject: Personally identifiable information from education records
records.obligation_summary: A vendor receiving education records under the school-official exception must be under the institution's direct control regarding use and maintenance, use the data only for the authorised purpose, and not re-disclose without authority.
records.source_statement_boundary: 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1) states the conditions of the school-official exception. The regulation addresses the institution's disclosure, not vendor conduct in the abstract.
records.ssls_interpretation: SSLS reads this as requiring purpose-bound processing, no secondary use, and contractual re-disclosure control before any real education record is accepted.
records.required_control: Purpose-bound data handling, documented direct-control terms, and enforced re-disclosure prohibition.
records.current_control: Zero-PII boundary: synthetic fixtures only, no persistence layer, no ingestion path.
records.mapped_work_package: Deferred to the work package that first proposes district data ingestion
records.evidence_requirement: Executed data-sharing agreement, purpose-binding design record, re-disclosure control evidence.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Contract artifact plus reviewed design record; automated evidence is insufficient.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with qualified legal review
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state only that it currently processes no education records.
records.prohibited_claim: FERPA compliant; FERPA ready; FERPA aligned
records.review_trigger: Before any district data-sharing agreement is signed
records.notes: The zero-PII boundary is what makes this NOT-APPLICABLE. The boundary is therefore a governed control, not an incidental fact.

records.title: Parental inspection and amendment of education records
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS holds education-record data on behalf of a district.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: A hosting vendor must be able to surface and correct records so the district can honour inspection and amendment requests.
records.subject: Access and amendment workflow
records.obligation_summary: Institutions must let parents and eligible students inspect records and request amendment of records believed inaccurate or misleading.
records.source_statement_boundary: The rights run against the educational agency or institution. The regulation imposes no direct vendor workflow.
records.ssls_interpretation: Any SSLS record store must be able to produce a complete per-student export and support a correction path with provenance, or the district cannot meet its own duty.
records.required_control: Per-subject record export and an auditable correction path with retained provenance.
records.current_control: Not built. The shared-object model defines record identity and relationships but no subject-access function exists.
records.mapped_work_package: Deferred to the first persistence work package
records.evidence_requirement: Demonstrated export and correction workflow against synthetic data.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated functional test plus reviewed walkthrough.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that subject-access capability is specified but not implemented.
records.notes: Recorded as a real design constraint on any future schema.

records.title: Protected-category survey notice and consent
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS administers or co-administers a survey, analysis or evaluation of students for a federally funded recipient, or collects student personal information for marketing.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. No student-facing instrument exists.
records.future_phase_applicability: Any screener, family survey or behavioural instrument delivered to students would need to be assessed against the protected categories.
records.subject: Student survey instruments
records.obligation_summary: Recipients must provide notice and obtain consent or offer opt-out before administering surveys revealing protected categories, and must allow inspection of instruments.
records.source_statement_boundary: Part 98 addresses the funded recipient. It contains no school-official style vendor exception.
records.ssls_interpretation: If SSLS ever builds a student-facing instrument, PPRA screening must occur at design time, not at deployment.
records.required_control: Design-time PPRA screening gate for any student-facing instrument.
records.current_control: None needed. No instrument capability exists.
records.mapped_work_package: Gate condition on any future assessment or survey capability
records.evidence_requirement: Screening record for each instrument.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Reviewed design record.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with qualified legal review
records.claim_implication: No claim available.
records.notes: Recorded because multilingual-learner screening is a plausible future capability.

records.title: IDEA confidentiality and destruction of special-education PII
records.applicability_trigger: A state or local education agency shares real Part B personally identifiable information with SSLS.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: Special-education program data carries a destruction duty once information is no longer needed to provide services.
records.subject: Part B personally identifiable information
records.obligation_summary: Agencies must protect confidentiality of Part B personally identifiable information consistent with FERPA and must address destruction of information no longer needed for services, with notice to parents.
records.source_statement_boundary: The duty is placed on the Secretary, state agencies and local agencies. The regulation does not bind vendors directly.
records.ssls_interpretation: Any special-education data model must carry a purge capability and a retention field from the first schema, because retrofitting deletion into a record system is not reliable.
records.required_control: Retention field and verified purge capability on any special-education record type.
records.current_control: None. No persistence exists.
records.evidence_requirement: Purge execution evidence against synthetic records.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated test with recorded artifact.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with qualified legal review
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.notes: Source currency is CONFLICTED (see SRC-004). Re-verification precedes any determination.

records.title: Verifiable parental consent for under-13 personal information
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS operates a child-directed service or gains actual knowledge of collecting personal information from a child under 13.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. There is no child-facing surface and no personal information of any kind is collected.
records.future_phase_applicability: A student-facing feature would trigger the amended rule, whose general compliance date is 2026-04-22.
records.subject: Personal information of children under 13
records.obligation_summary: Operators must give notice and obtain verifiable parental consent before collecting, using or disclosing personal information from children under 13, with a school-authorised consent pathway recognised by FTC guidance for school-supported services.
records.source_statement_boundary: The rule addresses operators of child-directed or actual-knowledge services. The school-consent pathway comes from FTC guidance interpreting the rule.
records.ssls_interpretation: Any student-facing surface must be treated as child-directed by default until a documented age-gating analysis says otherwise.
records.required_control: Consent architecture, age determination, and a documented child-directed analysis before student-facing launch.
records.current_control: No student-facing surface. Operator-only shell.
records.mapped_work_package: Gate condition on any student-facing capability
records.evidence_requirement: Child-directed determination record and consent-flow evidence.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Reviewed determination record plus functional evidence.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with qualified legal review
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that no personal information is collected from anyone.
records.review_trigger: Any proposal for a student-facing surface
records.review_date: 2026-04-22 is the external compliance date if triggered before then
records.notes: The nearest dated external trigger tracked by WP-038, and it is conditional, not automatic.

records.title: Written data retention and deletion policy for children's data
records.applicability_trigger: Same trigger as OBL-005.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: A written retention policy with defined deletion timing becomes mandatory, not optional.
records.subject: Retention of children's personal information
records.obligation_summary: Operators must maintain a written retention policy, keep children's personal information only as long as reasonably necessary for the collection purpose, and delete it thereafter with reasonable disposal protection.
records.source_statement_boundary: This is a new requirement added by the 2025 amendments.
records.ssls_interpretation: Retention must be a declared field on any child-related record type rather than an operational habit.
records.required_control: Declared retention period per record type and evidenced deletion.
records.current_control: No data retained. Fixtures are compile-time constants.
records.evidence_requirement: Written policy artifact plus deletion execution evidence.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Policy document plus automated deletion test.
records.claim_implication: None available.

records.title: Massachusetts student-record security and duty-limited vendor access
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education
records.applicability_trigger: A Massachusetts district grants SSLS access to student records under a service contract.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: Access must be limited to what the vendor's duties require and computerised systems must be electronically secure.
records.subject: Massachusetts student records
records.obligation_summary: Contracted service providers may be authorised school personnel with access limited to their duties, and the district must ensure computerised systems holding records are electronically secure.
records.source_statement_boundary: The duty is placed on the principal, superintendent and school committee. The regulation does not create a direct vendor duty or penalty.
records.ssls_interpretation: Duty-limited access is a schema and authorization requirement, not a contract clause alone. The SSLS authorization model already separates capacity, relationship, purpose and scope, which is the right shape for this.
records.required_control: Role and purpose scoped access enforced in the data layer, not only in the interface.
records.current_control: Authorization model specified in the shared-object architecture; no runtime enforcement exists because there is no data layer.
records.mapped_work_package: First persistence and authentication work package
records.evidence_requirement: Enforced policy evidence at the data layer.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated authorization tests plus reviewed policy definitions.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that an authorization model is specified and unimplemented.
records.notes: Vendor exposure here is contractual, and the district holds the regulatory duty.

records.title: Massachusetts student-record destruction timelines
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Board of Elementary and Secondary Education
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS stores Massachusetts student-record data for a district.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: Transcript data is destroyable only after sixty years; the temporary record must be destroyed no later than seven years after transfer, graduation or withdrawal, with prior written notice.
records.subject: Record retention periods
records.obligation_summary: Sets differentiated destruction timelines for the transcript and the temporary record, and requires written notice before destruction.
records.source_statement_boundary: 603 CMR 23.06 states the timelines. It addresses the district as record custodian.
records.ssls_interpretation: A single blanket retention setting cannot satisfy this. Record types must carry independent retention classes from the first schema.
records.required_control: Per-record-type retention class with a scheduled destruction path and pre-destruction notice hook.
records.current_control: None. No stored records.
records.evidence_requirement: Retention class definitions plus destruction execution evidence.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated test plus reviewed schedule.
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.notes: This is the clearest example of an obligation that must shape schema design long before it applies.

records.title: Written comprehensive information security program
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS owns, licenses, receives, stores, maintains, processes or otherwise has access to a Massachusetts resident's name combined with a Social Security number, driver's licence or state ID number, or financial account number.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. No such data element is held, including for the operator.
records.future_phase_applicability: Triggers directly on the vendor, independently of any district contract. Employment or payment records could trigger it before any student data does.
records.subject: Personal information of Massachusetts residents
records.obligation_summary: Requires a written information security program with designated responsibility, risk assessment, employee policy, access control on termination, service-provider oversight, monitoring, annual review and incident documentation.
records.source_statement_boundary: 201 CMR 17.01 states the scope and 17.03 enumerates the program elements. Personal information is narrowly defined at 17.02.
records.ssls_interpretation: This is the most likely first binding security obligation on SSLS, and it may arrive through payroll or payment data rather than student data.
records.required_control: A written information security program with the enumerated elements.
records.current_control: None. No written program exists. Technical controls exist in the evidence pipeline but they are not a program.
records.mapped_work_package: Routed to the security work package; must precede any handling of narrow personal information
records.evidence_requirement: The written program plus annual review record.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Document artifact with owner acceptance; automated evidence cannot satisfy this.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that no Massachusetts-defined personal information is held.
records.review_trigger: First handling of narrow personal information, including operator payroll or payment data
records.notes: Named as a gap because the trigger is closer than the student-data triggers.

records.title: Encryption and access control for personal information
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation
records.applicability_trigger: Same trigger as OBL-009 where the information is on a computer system.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: Requires secure authentication, access control, and encryption of personal information in transit across public networks and on portable devices.
records.subject: Computer system security requirements
records.obligation_summary: Sets technical requirements including secure user authentication, access control, encryption in transit and on portable devices, monitoring and up-to-date protective software.
records.source_statement_boundary: 17.04 enumerates the requirements. Subsections beyond (1) to (3) were not fully enumerated during WP-038 verification.
records.ssls_interpretation: These requirements shape the authentication design that SSLS does not yet have, so the design should be specified before it is needed.
records.required_control: Authenticated access with enforced transport encryption and device controls.
records.current_control: No authentication exists. The published surface is a public read-only prototype served over HTTPS with no accounts and no personal information.
records.evidence_requirement: Configuration evidence and authentication tests.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated evidence plus reviewed configuration record.
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.notes: Clause-level enumeration of 17.04 is incomplete and recorded as a verification gap.

records.title: District web and mobile accessibility conformance to WCAG 2.1 AA
records.source_version: Final rule 2024, dates extended by 2026 interim final rule
records.applicability_trigger: A public entity uses SSLS as part of its web content or mobile services.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not directly applicable. SSLS is not a public entity. The obligation reaches SSLS only through a district's own duty and its procurement terms.
records.future_phase_applicability: Districts must conform by 2027-04-26 for populations of fifty thousand or more, and 2028-04-26 for smaller populations and special district governments.
records.subject: Web content and mobile applications used by public entities
records.obligation_summary: Public entities must make web content and mobile applications conform to WCAG 2.1 Level AA, subject to listed exceptions and limited defences.
records.source_statement_boundary: The regulated party is the public entity. The rule does not regulate private vendors.
records.ssls_interpretation: Because the customer's duty is dated and non-negotiable, SSLS treats WCAG conformance as a product requirement now rather than a procurement surprise later. SSLS builds to WCAG 2.2 AA, which is a superset of the 2.1 AA criteria named in the rule.
records.required_control: Verified conformance testing against the named criteria, with the internal target stated as a version.
records.current_control: ULW-AS-001 v1.3 internal standard applied across the shell, with automated axe-core checks in the test suite. Automated checks cover only part of the criteria set.
records.evidence_requirement: Manual and assistive-technology testing evidence in addition to automated checks.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated scan plus documented manual testing. Independent audit is required before any external conformance statement.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with independent accessibility review before any external statement
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that it applies an internal accessibility standard and runs automated checks. It may not state conformance.
records.prohibited_claim: WCAG compliant; WCAG certified; ADA compliant; accessible
records.review_trigger: Before any accessibility statement is published or any procurement response is submitted
records.notes: Automated coverage is partial by nature. Recorded as PARTIAL rather than IMPLEMENTED for that reason.

records.title: Internal conformance target version
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS publishes a user interface.
records.current_phase_applicability: Applies now as an internal engineering target, not as a legal duty.
records.future_phase_applicability: Remains the internal target unless a regulation names a different version.
records.subject: Internal accessibility target
records.obligation_summary: WCAG 2.2 is the current W3C Recommendation and its Level AA criteria form a superset of the WCAG 2.1 AA criteria named in ADA Title II and the HHS Section 504 rule.
records.source_statement_boundary: W3C states version status and conformance levels. W3C does not impose a legal duty.
records.ssls_interpretation: Targeting 2.2 AA satisfies the 2.1 AA criteria named in regulation and avoids a re-test cycle. This is an engineering decision, recorded as such, and it creates no conformance claim.
records.required_control: A single declared internal target version applied consistently across the design system.
records.current_control: ULW-AS-001 v1.3 is the internal standard. Its stated relationship to a specific WCAG version is not recorded in a single canonical place.
records.evidence_requirement: A recorded decision naming the target version and its relationship to ULW-AS-001.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Owner decision record.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state which version it builds toward. It may not state that it meets it.
records.review_trigger: Publication of any accessibility conformance report
records.notes: Raised as a decision candidate for the owner because the internal standard and the external version are not yet formally bound.

records.title: Accessibility conformance report as self-disclosure
records.applicability_trigger: A district or state procurement asks for an accessibility conformance report.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. No procurement response has been made.
records.future_phase_applicability: A completed report will be requested in most district procurements.
records.subject: Accessibility conformance reporting
records.obligation_summary: The template is a vendor self-disclosure. Completing it produces an Accessibility Conformance Report, and no accreditation or certification attaches to the process.
records.source_statement_boundary: ITI describes the template as a reporting template and never as a certification.
records.ssls_interpretation: Any SSLS report must state its testing method and its limits on its face, because a self-disclosure that reads like a certification is a misleading claim.
records.required_control: A report template that declares method, scope, date and independence status.
records.current_control: None produced.
records.evidence_requirement: The completed report plus its underlying test evidence.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Documented manual and automated testing.
records.claim_implication: A report may be described as a self-disclosure only.

records.obligation_summary: Harmonises ICT accessibility requirements for European public-sector web and procurement obligations.
records.source_statement_boundary: ETSI publishes the harmonised standard; the legal force comes from EU directives.
records.ssls_interpretation: Recorded to close the question rather than leave it unexamined.

records.title: Software bill of materials production
records.citation: NTIA minimum elements for an SBOM
records.applicability_trigger: Federal software procurement, or a district or state procurement that asks for an SBOM.
records.current_phase_applicability: Reference. SSLS produces an SBOM voluntarily through the WP-037 evidence pipeline.
records.future_phase_applicability: Becomes a procurement condition in federal sales and increasingly in state procurement.
records.subject: Dependency transparency
records.obligation_summary: Defines the baseline SBOM data fields including author, timestamp, supplier, component name and version, and dependency relationships.
records.source_statement_boundary: NTIA defines minimum elements. The document is guidance and does not itself bind private parties.

records.title: Dependency vulnerability identification and remediation
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS maintains a software product with third-party dependencies.
records.current_phase_applicability: Applies now as an adopted internal practice. It is not a legal duty.
records.future_phase_applicability: Becomes a procurement expectation in district and state security reviews.
records.subject: Third-party dependency risk
records.obligation_summary: Recommends continuous identification and remediation of vulnerabilities in software assets.
records.source_statement_boundary: CIS publishes voluntary safeguards. Adoption is elective.
records.ssls_interpretation: SSLS treats this as an internal operating rule because it is cheap now and expensive to retrofit.
records.required_control: Repeatable dependency advisory scan with recorded triage and remediation.
records.current_control: Pipeline advisory scan via the npm bulk advisory endpoint, with WP-037 triage, remediation and post-remediation rescan recorded as EV-021 to EV-025.

records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated scan with retained artifacts; single-source and point-in-time.

records.prohibited_claim: No vulnerabilities; secure dependencies; independently validated
records.review_date: Evidence expires seven days after production
records.notes: bun audit remains unable to complete in the environment. That limitation is preserved in EV-VULN.

records.title: Dependency licence posture
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS distributes or hosts software containing third-party components.

records.future_phase_applicability: Becomes a procurement and legal review input at first commercial distribution.

records.obligation_summary: Provides standard identifiers and a data model for communicating component licence information.

records.title: Independent security attestation expectation
records.source_version: TSC 2017 with 2022 revised points of focus
records.applicability_trigger: A district or state procurement requires an independent attestation for a hosted service.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. No hosted service handling customer data exists.
records.future_phase_applicability: A Type 2 report requires an observation period of several months, so the lead time must be planned before a launch date is promised.

records.ssls_interpretation: The observation window is the real constraint, not the audit itself.

records.current_control: None. No attestation has been sought.
records.mapped_work_package: Unassigned; sequencing decision required before any launch commitment

records.prohibited_claim: SOC 2 certified; SOC 2 compliant; audit ready
records.review_trigger: Before any launch date is committed to a district
records.notes: ISO/IEC 27001 certification is an alternative market path with the same character: independent and not yet sought.

records.title: AI risk management before any AI feature
records.applicability_trigger: An AI feature is proposed for SSLS.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. The program prohibits AI features in the current phase.
records.future_phase_applicability: A govern, map, measure and manage cycle would need to exist before, not after, a first AI feature.
records.subject: AI risk management
records.obligation_summary: Voluntary process guidance for governing, mapping, measuring and managing AI risks. It is neither mandatory nor certifiable.
records.source_statement_boundary: NIST states the framework is voluntary. A revision is in progress.
records.ssls_interpretation: The existing value-stream AI gating rules are the placeholder for this. They are refusal rules, not a risk-management program.
records.required_control: An AI risk process bound to a gate that precedes any model integration.
records.current_control: Prohibition. AI features are refused in the current phase and the refusal is encoded in the value-stream gates.
records.mapped_work_package: Gate condition on any AI capability
records.evidence_requirement: Risk process artifact plus per-feature records.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Reviewed documentation.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that it has no AI features.
records.prohibited_claim: NIST AI RMF aligned; responsible AI certified
records.notes: NIST AI 600-1 and ISO/IEC 42001 travel with this obligation as reference sources.

records.title: Existing law applies to AI claims and behaviour
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS makes any public statement about AI capability, including a statement about future capability.
records.current_phase_applicability: Applies now to marketing and public-surface language even though no AI feature exists.
records.future_phase_applicability: Applies with greater force once any AI feature ships.
records.subject: AI-related representations
records.obligation_summary: Existing Massachusetts consumer protection, anti-discrimination and data security law applies to developers, suppliers and users of AI, and the advisory creates no new AI-specific statute.
records.source_statement_boundary: The Attorney General states how existing law applies. The advisory is guidance interpreting statutes such as c. 93A.
records.ssls_interpretation: Claim discipline is a legal control, not a style preference. The Claims Register is the operating control for this obligation.
records.required_control: A maintained claims register with prohibited wording, applied to every public surface.
records.current_control: Claims Register CLM-001 to CLM-013 with recorded prohibited claims, plus a refused-claims boundary surface in the application.
records.mapped_work_package: Maintained across all work packages; established in WP-000
records.evidence_requirement: The register plus review of published surfaces against it.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Reviewed register with per-surface check.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that it maintains a claims register and refuses specified claims.
records.review_trigger: Every published change to a public surface
records.notes: This is one of the few obligations that applies right now to the current build.

records.title: Developer-directed AI design expectations
records.source_authority: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Educational Technology
records.citation: Designing for Education with AI: An Essential Guide for Developers
records.applicability_trigger: Any AI capability design.
records.current_phase_applicability: Reference. Explicitly non-regulatory.
records.future_phase_applicability: Would inform design review for any AI capability.
records.subject: AI design practice in education
records.obligation_summary: Non-regulatory recommendations for developers on evidence, transparency, human oversight and equity in educational AI.
records.source_statement_boundary: The Department states the guidance is non-regulatory and that examples are not endorsements.
records.ssls_interpretation: Its emphasis on evidence-bound output and human review matches the SSLS rule that AI output must be reviewable and never autonomously decide.
records.required_control: Human review requirement on any AI-produced output.
records.current_control: Encoded as a refusal rule: no autonomous high-impact decisions, and no AI features in this phase.
records.mapped_work_package: Gate condition on any AI capability
records.evidence_requirement: Design record per AI feature.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Reviewed design record.
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.prohibited_claim: Department of Education endorsed; ED aligned

records.title: Colorado automated decision-making watch item
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS develops or deploys a high-risk automated decision-making system affecting Colorado residents on or after 2027-01-01.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not applicable. The law is not yet effective and there is no Colorado presence or automated decision capability.
records.future_phase_applicability: Would impose developer and deployer duties including impact assessment and consumer disclosure.
records.subject: Automated consequential decisions
records.obligation_summary: Signed 2026-05-14, replacing the 2024 Colorado AI Act with a narrower framework effective 2027-01-01.
records.source_statement_boundary: The bill text states the effective date. Its scope was narrowed relative to SB 24-205.
records.ssls_interpretation: Tracked because a governed learner-record product that recommended placement or eligibility could fall within a consequential-decision definition.
records.required_control: None yet. A scope determination at the point any recommendation capability is proposed.
records.current_control: Not applicable. No automated decision capability exists.
records.evidence_requirement: Scope determination record if triggered.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Reviewed determination with legal input.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with qualified legal review
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.review_trigger: Any recommendation or eligibility-scoring capability, or Colorado market entry
records.notes: Recorded as ADOPTED-NOT-YET-EFFECTIVE at source level to prevent a present-tense obligation.

records.title: Roster and enrolment data exchange
records.applicability_trigger: A district needs to sync students, organisations, classes or enrolments into SSLS.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered. No ingestion path exists.
records.future_phase_applicability: Required in practice for any district pilot that must load a real roster.
records.subject: Roster interoperability
records.obligation_summary: Standardises exchange of roster, course and grade data through CSV bulk and REST modes. Certification is granted only after passing the test suite.
records.source_statement_boundary: 1EdTech publishes the specification and operates the certification programme.
records.ssls_interpretation: Roster shape should constrain the shared-object student model now, so that a later adapter is a mapping rather than a migration.
records.required_control: Student and enrolment models compatible with OneRoster entities.
records.current_control: Shared-object model defines student-adjacent object types but no OneRoster mapping exists.
records.evidence_requirement: Mapping document plus certification if conformance is ever claimed.
records.minimum_evidence_method: 1EdTech certification for any conformance statement; internal mapping evidence otherwise.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that no roster integration exists.
records.prohibited_claim: OneRoster conformant; OneRoster certified; OneRoster compatible
records.notes: Implementing a specification informally is not certified conformance.

records.title: Program and service data exchange with state systems
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS must exchange multilingual-learner or special-education program data with a district or state system.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: State-level adoption makes this the primary path for program and compliance reporting data.
records.subject: Program participation and service data
records.obligation_summary: A community-governed K-12 data model and API. Conformance is verified through community testing rather than a paid certification badge.
records.source_statement_boundary: The Ed-Fi Alliance publishes the standard and its testing tools.
records.ssls_interpretation: Program participation, service delivery and eligibility concepts should be named against Ed-Fi domains at first modelling, not renamed later.
records.required_control: Domain naming aligned to Ed-Fi program and student domains.
records.current_control: No program data model exists.
records.evidence_requirement: Mapping document plus community conformance testing if claimed.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Community conformance testing for any conformance statement.
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.notes: Named MISSING rather than NOT-APPLICABLE because the product concept depends on this data class.

records.title: Deferred interoperability specifications
records.citation: LTI 1.3 with Advantage services; QTI 3.0.1; Caliper 1.2; CASE 1.1; Common Cartridge 1.4
records.applicability_trigger: LMS embedding, assessment item exchange, analytics event emission, competency framework exchange or content packaging.
records.current_phase_applicability: Reference only. None of these capabilities exists or is planned in the current phase.
records.future_phase_applicability: LTI Advantage and Caliper become relevant on LMS embedding or analytics emission. QTI, CASE and Common Cartridge remain out of scope for a governed learner-record product.
records.subject: Learning platform interoperability
records.obligation_summary: Specification family covering tool launch and grade passback, assessment item exchange, analytics events, competency frameworks and content packaging.
records.source_statement_boundary: 1EdTech publishes each specification and operates certification programmes.
records.ssls_interpretation: Recorded as deferred so that later scope conversations start from a written position rather than an open field.
records.required_control: None at present.
records.current_control: Not applicable.
records.evidence_requirement: None.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Not applicable.
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.prohibited_claim: LTI Advantage certified; QTI conformant; Caliper conformant
records.review_trigger: LMS embedding or analytics emission proposal
records.notes: Release dates for several of these specifications were not confirmed. Only versions are recorded.

records.title: District data privacy agreement execution
records.citation: TEC Student Data Privacy Alliance; SDPC National Data Privacy Agreement
records.applicability_trigger: A Massachusetts district or collaborative requires an executed data privacy agreement before tool use.
records.current_phase_applicability: Not triggered.
records.future_phase_applicability: This is the most likely first contractual gate for a Massachusetts pilot, and it will import terms that exceed regulation.
records.subject: Vendor data privacy agreement
records.obligation_summary: Districts and collaboratives require vendors to sign a standard data privacy agreement before tools that collect student personal information are used.
records.source_statement_boundary: These are private contract templates, not law.
records.ssls_interpretation: The agreement, not the regulation, is what will actually bind SSLS first. Preparing for it is a product requirement, not a legal one.
records.required_control: Ability to answer the standard agreement's data-inventory, subprocessor, deletion and breach questions with evidence.
records.current_control: No agreement has been reviewed and no subprocessor inventory exists.
records.mapped_work_package: Routed to the pilot-readiness work package
records.evidence_requirement: Executed agreement plus supporting inventories.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Contract artifact.
records.owner_candidate: Founder / Operator, with qualified legal review
records.claim_implication: None available.
records.prohibited_claim: SDPC approved; district approved; DPA in place
records.review_trigger: First district conversation that reaches procurement
records.notes: Template version UNVERIFIED at source level.

records.title: Accuracy of public claims on the published prototype
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Office of the Attorney General
records.citation: AGO AI Advisory; M.G.L. c. 93A as referenced therein
records.applicability_trigger: A public surface exists at a reachable URL.
records.current_phase_applicability: Applies now. A public prototype is published and reachable.
records.future_phase_applicability: Applies with greater consequence as commercial intent becomes explicit.
records.subject: Public representations
records.obligation_summary: Consumer protection law applies to representations made about a product, including capability, security, privacy and compliance statements.
records.source_statement_boundary: The advisory states that existing consumer protection law applies. It does not enumerate product wording.
records.ssls_interpretation: Publication is not release, and the published surface must say so. Every status shown must be traceable to a recorded fact.
records.required_control: Publication boundary statement plus traceable status rendering.
records.current_control: PUBLIC PROTOTYPE boundary recorded in WP-037, refused-claims surface in the application, and authority never derived from implementation status.
records.evidence_requirement: Reachability evidence plus surface review against the claims register.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Recorded evidence plus human review.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may describe the published surface as a public prototype that is not a release.
records.prohibited_claim: Production ready; district ready; live product

records.title: Zero personal data on the current surface
records.source_authority: Massachusetts Office of Consumer Affairs and Business Regulation
records.applicability_trigger: The scope test is continuous: the obligation attaches the moment personal information is received.
records.current_phase_applicability: Applies now as a boundary to hold, not as a duty being discharged. The current surface collects nothing.
records.future_phase_applicability: The moment any form, account or analytics capture is added, OBL-009 to OBL-012 attach.
records.subject: Data collection on the public surface
records.obligation_summary: The regulation attaches to any person that receives, stores, maintains, processes or has access to personal information about a Massachusetts resident.
records.source_statement_boundary: 17.01 states the scope. It does not describe web surfaces specifically.
records.ssls_interpretation: Keeping the collection surface empty is the cheapest available control, and it must be verified rather than assumed.
records.required_control: Verified absence of collection: no accounts, no forms that transmit, no analytics, no third-party trackers.
records.current_control: Verified at WP-038: no authentication, no submitting forms, no analytics or tracking scripts, no third-party data calls. One first-party sidebar preference cookie is set by the interface. Platform error reporting is invoked only if the host injects it.
records.evidence_requirement: Repeatable scan of the source tree for collection paths.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Automated boundary scan plus code review.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that the current surface collects no personal information and sets one first-party preference cookie.
records.prohibited_claim: Privacy compliant; no cookies; no tracking of any kind
records.review_trigger: Any added form, account, analytics or third-party script
records.notes: The sidebar preference cookie is recorded rather than omitted, because a no-cookies claim would be inaccurate.

records.title: Branch protection and change-control enforcement
records.applicability_trigger: SSLS maintains a repository that is the authorised software source of truth.
records.current_phase_applicability: Applies now as an internal practice.
records.future_phase_applicability: Becomes an evidence question in any security review.
records.subject: Change control
records.obligation_summary: Recommends controlled change processes for application software, including review and enforcement of protections.
records.source_statement_boundary: CIS publishes voluntary safeguards.
records.ssls_interpretation: A workflow that exists is not an enforcement that is configured. The distinction is already recorded as FND-012.
records.required_control: Verified branch protection requiring the evidence and binding checks to pass.
records.current_control: CI workflows exist. Branch-protection enforcement is not verified.
records.evidence_requirement: Repository settings evidence.
records.minimum_evidence_method: Configuration evidence from the hosting platform.
records.claim_implication: SSLS may state that CI workflows exist and that enforcement is unverified.
records.prohibited_claim: Enforced change control; protected main branch
records.notes: Carried from WP-037 rather than restated as a new finding.
